booklets: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 6 Extension 1/Further Applications of Calculus 1_Multiplicity of zeroes of polynomial functions.md
firstRoundFindings: quiz.q8: The fourth option's why incorrectly states that $P''(2)=0$. It equals $98$; the explanation must use $P'(2)=0$ to establish that $2$ is repeated, or use $P''(-\dfrac{3}{2})=98$ to rule out a triple zero there.

theory: The procedure needs to include testing rational candidates for non-monic polynomials: integer factors of the constant term alone can miss the repeated zero, as in practice.development[0], practice.development[1] and quiz.q8. It also needs to distinguish a lower bound on multiplicity from exact multiplicity: continue derivative tests until the first non-zero derivative, or use the degree to establish that the known multiplicities exhaust the polynomial. The statement that all zero multiplicities sum to the degree requires counting complex zeroes as well; without that qualification it is false for real zeroes.
summary: Repaired the theory to include rational candidates for non-monic polynomials, distinguish lower bounds from exact multiplicities, and count complex zeroes in the degree statement; updated affected procedure headings and clarified the degree argument in practice.development[0]. Corrected quiz.q8's fourth-option explanation using $P'(2)=0$, preserving all questions, values and calculations and removing no whole items.
reviewSummary: All 17 practice items and eight quiz questions have correct answers, usable working and booklet-supported question types; every quiz has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations. The theory correctly explains derivative multiplicity tests and sums and products of zeroes, and no worked examples or removals were supplied.
